claim: The board's whole premise is that a notification's jump target can be deleted, leaving the row behind with a 'This page was deleted' marker.
truth: Nothing in the product ever nulls an existing actionUrl — it is written once at creation and never updated, and deleting a page or site does not touch it. What actually renders this state is a notification CREATED with no actionUrl, and that is 5 of the 7 producible types: all four SECURITY_* notifications and PAYMENT_FAILED. So the strip saying 'What this points to was deleted' is shown over 'Your password was changed', which is a false statement the product makes about itself.
evidence: NotificationPanel.tsx:258 `const jumpable = n.actionUrl != null;` is the only test, and :290-299 renders the warning strip on the else branch. actionUrl is written only at creation — notification.trigger.ts:42 inside prisma.notification.create — and a repo-wide grep for actionUrl across server/, packages/dashboard/ and lib/ finds no update or nulling anywhere. Creation sites with no actionUrl: account.service.ts:28,49,378,415 (SECURITY_PASSWORD_CHANGED ×2, SECURITY_2FA_CHANGED ×2) and stripe-webhook.service.ts:64 (PAYMENT_FAILED). Sites with one: auth.ts:328 '/dashboard/settings/team', form-submission.service.ts:58 and workers/publish/[jobId]/route.ts:162,217 '/dashboard/sites/${siteId}'.
edit: Rename 165:71 to 'Notifications · no-jump-target (a notification created without one — every security and payment notification)' and change the strip copy per FIG-L-22. Replace the sample row with one the code can produce, e.g. 'Two-factor authentication was enabled on your account'. The 'deleted target' story has no producer and must not be the board's premise.

claim: Section 20 has 107 inbound cross-module edges and 5 outbound, all into Journeys — the most-linked-to small section in the file and almost never linking onward.
truth: That is not a wiring oversight, it is the product: every click in this panel LEAVES the editor. A row's jump is a full-page navigation to the dashboard, and only two non-null actionUrl shapes exist in the whole codebase. Nothing a notification points at is inside this Figma file, which is why the section has almost no outbound edges. The one destination that can be drawn is the full list, which does exist.

claim: The family draws an all-unread list (165:2) and an all-read list (165:24) and nothing between them.
truth: The mixed list is the most common screen in the product, and it has a specific order the two extremes cannot show: unread rows are sorted to the top, then everything is newest-first. The instant you read one row it drops below the remaining unread ones, so a mixed panel is what you see for the rest of the session.
evidence: NotificationPanel.tsx:170-173 `const ordered = [...rows].sort((a, b) => { if (a.read !== b.read) return a.read ? 1 : -1; return new Date(b.createdAt).getTime() - new Date(a.createdAt).getTime(); });`. Read rows render `bk-notif-row` with a spacer where the dot was (:271-272); unread render `bk-notif-row--unread` with a StatusDot (:274). Day bands are computed on the SORTED order (:254-255), so a read row from today can sit under a band below an unread row from yesterday.
edit: Clone 165:2 at 280×812 as 'Notifications · mixed (unread first, then newest)': two unread rows with tint + dot at the top under 'TODAY', then two read rows with the spacer and no tint, and show a day band appearing a second time below the read boundary. Add a caption naming the sort: unread first, then newest — so the bands can repeat.

claim: The reference board is named 'Reference · toast catalog — 5 tones · sticky class'.
truth: '5 tones' is correct. 'sticky class' is not — there is no sticky class, variant or visual treatment. Stickiness is a numeric property on the toast input (duration: Infinity), and a sticky toast is pixel-identical to a 5-second one. Five call sites use it. The board therefore promises a visual distinction the design system does not have.
